# Applying the patches

<!-- Generated by `node src/report.js` from results/apply/*.json. Do not edit. -->

Of the 248 vectors, 210 are patches in the plain sense: the vector records the file tree before and the file tree after, and the diff is what git or GNU diff printed for the two. For each of them the old tree is written to an empty directory, the program under test applies the diff there, and the directory is read back and compared with the new tree, byte for byte, file modes and symbolic links included. A library that patches one file at a time is given each file section together with the old content of that file.

There are four ways this can end:

| | the program said | and the files are |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **right** | done | exactly the new tree |
| **refused** | error | untouched |
| **left half-done** | error | changed, and not the new tree |
| **wrong** | done | not the new tree |

**Read this first.**

- "Refused" is a limitation: the caller is told, and nothing is lost. "Wrong" is the column that matters — a file with different content, a file that should be gone, a file that is gone and should not be, and no error to say so.
- This is not a ranking. The corpus collects hard cases; every one of these programs applies an ordinary patch correctly.
- Every diff here is unmodified output of git or GNU diff, applied to exactly the tree it was made from. Nothing is fuzzy, offset or already applied.
- The invocation is in the table. Other options give other results; `git apply --unidiff-zero` is listed next to `git apply` to show one such case.
- The versions are the ones installed where this was run. What was already known to each project is in [`FINDINGS.md`](FINDINGS.md).

The reference appliers are part of this repository (`src/refapply.js`, `reference/python/udiff_reference.py`). They are in the table to show that every one of these patches can be applied from its text and the old files alone. A library that patches one file at a time is not given the vectors in which no file content changes (pure renames, mode changes), a library that takes text is not given files that are not valid UTF-8, libgit2 is not given what GNU diff wrote, and patch-package, pnpm and Yarn, which always remove `a/` and `b/` and take no `-p`, are given only the vectors of the `git` and `git-config` tiers whose names carry those two prefixes. That is why the number of patches differs.

### git-apply

git apply 2.43.0 · C · <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-apply>

- Under test: `git apply -pN FILE` — on a directory
- No options beyond -p. git apply is all or nothing.

### gnu-patch

GNU patch 2.7.6 · C · <https://savannah.gnu.org/projects/patch/>

- Under test: `patch -pN -f --no-backup-if-mismatch -i FILE` — on a directory
- -f: never ask. --no-backup-if-mismatch: no .orig files next to a file patched with fuzz or at an offset, so that only what patch did to the files themselves is compared. Rejects (.rej) are left where patch puts them.

197 of 210 patches are applied correctly.

### bsd-patch

BSD patch 2.0-12u11 FreeBSD · C · <https://cgit.freebsd.org/src/tree/usr.bin/patch>

- Under test: `patch -pN -f -s -E -V none -i FILE` — on a directory
- -f: never ask. -s: print only what went wrong. -E: remove a file that is empty after patching; without it a file the patch deletes is left as an empty file, and the ports framework of FreeBSD passes it too (Mk/bsd.port.mk, PATCH_ARGS). -V none: no FILE.orig next to every patched file (made unless --posix is given), so that only what patch did to the files themselves is compared. Rejects (.rej) are left where patch puts them.

### libgit2

libgit2 1.9.7 (via pygit2 1.21.0) · C · <https://libgit2.org/>

- Under test: `Diff.parse_diff, then Repository.apply (git_diff_from_buffer, git_apply)` — on a directory
- Applied to the working directory (GIT_APPLY_LOCATION_WORKDIR). git_apply needs a repository: an empty one is initialised in the directory first; committing the files beforehand makes no difference to the results. git_diff_from_buffer reads names with one leading component (a/, b/); the adapter declines other vectors.

### patch-package

patch-package 8.0.1 · JavaScript · <https://github.com/ds300/patch-package>

- Under test: `parsePatchFile() + executeEffects(), as applyPatch() calls them` — on a directory
- The steps of applyPatch() in dist/applyPatches.js: read the file (readFileSync().toString(), so as UTF-8), parse it, a dry run, the real run; when that fails, a patch whose reverse would apply is taken to be applied already and counts as success. patch-package makes its patches with `git diff --src-prefix=a/ --dst-prefix=b/` and takes no -p: it always removes a/ and b/, so only vectors with those prefixes are given. readPatch() exits the process on a parse error; the adapter calls the parser itself and reports the error instead.

### jsdiff

jsdiff 9.0.0 · JavaScript · <https://github.com/kpdecker/jsdiff>

- Under test: `applyPatch(source, patch)` — one file at a time
- Default options (fuzzFactor 0, autoConvertLineEndings on). applyPatch returns false when a hunk does not fit.

All 185 patches are applied correctly.

### whatthepatch

whatthepatch 1.0.7 · Python · <https://github.com/cscorley/whatthepatch>

- Under test: `apply_diff(diff, old_text)  with diff from parse_patch(text)` — one file at a time
- It returns a list of lines; whether the last line ends with a newline is not part of its answer and is not compared.
- The pure-Python path (use_patch=False, the default). The lines it returns are joined with LF, as the library does itself where it writes them out (apply.py).

173 of 185 patches are applied correctly.

### java-diff-utils

java-diff-utils 4.18 · Java · <https://github.com/java-diff-utils/java-diff-utils>

- Under test: `UnifiedDiffReader.parseUnifiedDiff(stream).getFiles().get(0).getPatch().applyTo(lines)` — one file at a time
- It returns a list of lines; whether the last line ends with a newline is not part of its answer and is not compared.
- The old text is cut into lines the way the reader cuts the patch (BufferedReader.readLine), and the lines that come back are joined with LF.
